levelMapping: MTS-1 (0-2 YOE) -> MTS-2 (2-4 YOE) -> Computer Scientist 1 (~4-7 YOE, but 3-5 YOE offers are common) -> CS-2 (6-9 YOE). CS1/CS2 ≈ Google L4; with ~3.3 YOE expect MTS-2 or CS-1 depending on team and interview performance — confirm the level with the recruiter, and note at least one report of the role being changed from CS-1 to MTS-2 mid-process.

process.summary: Recruiter call, then (mostly for campus/early-career, occasionally for laterals) a HackerRank OA, then 3-5 strictly eliminatory one-hour rounds: 1-2 DSA rounds that mix in C++/Java/OS/DBMS fundamentals, a design round (LLD/OOD is more common than HLD at MTS-2/CS-1; HLD appears for CS-2), a hiring-manager/techno-managerial round (projects + more coding), and a final Director round (behavioral + a puzzle and/or an open-ended design/implementation task) that is the real decision point. India (Noida/Bengaluru) loops often run as single-day hiring drives with the next round scheduled within minutes of clearing the previous one. The loop's character: easy-medium LeetCode coding but deep language internals — C++ teams (Illustrator, Acrobat, Photoshop) grill smart pointers, move semantics, vtables, singletons and mutexes in every round; Java/backend teams run a dedicated concurrency round.

rounds.name: Recruiter screen
rounds.what: Background, notice period, CTC, team mapping; recruiters often cannot say what later rounds cover because panels decide round content at runtime based on previous-round feedback (confirmed by an Adobe employee on Blind).
rounds.probes: Ask explicitly for the level (MTS-2 vs CS-1) and the team's primary language — C++ teams and Java teams run very different loops; also ask whether the design round is LLD or HLD.

rounds.name: Online assessment
rounds.what: HackerRank. For campus/early-career: aptitude + technical MCQs (C/C++/Java output, OOP, OS, DBMS) + 1-2 coding problems. Laterals usually skip it, but one 2025 CS-2 candidate got a HackerRank OA with 2 medium DSA (sliding window, graph traversal) plus a small design-coding task (implement an LRU cache).
rounds.probes: Clean modular code; medium array/string/graph problems.

rounds.name: DSA round 1
rounds.what: 1-2 LeetCode easy-medium problems (arrays, strings, trees, sliding window, DP) coded in your own IDE or HackerRank CodePair, usually run against the interviewer's test cases. Several interviewers demand the optimal solution directly and bug-free code on the first attempt; some accept pseudo-code (team dependent). 10-15 min of C++/Java fundamentals are commonly mixed in (vector vs list, map internals, vtable, smart pointers; or Java threads/locks).
rounds.probes: Multiple approaches for the same problem (brute -> better -> optimal, and for DP: recursion -> memo -> tabulation -> space-optimized, all coded); variants and follow-ups on the same code; dry runs and complexity.

rounds.name: DSA round 2
rounds.what: Second coding round, often heavier on language internals: C++ smart pointers/move-semantics code snippets to fix, memory-leak examples, OS questions (virtual memory, paging, mutex vs semaphore), DBMS (indexing, sharding, SQL vs NoSQL, JDBC) — plus 1-2 more coding problems.
rounds.probes: 'Will this compile and why', output-prediction and debugging snippets; concurrency scenarios (two functions printing in order using mutexes, reader-writer); for Java roles a dedicated concurrency round (implement schedulers/concurrent structures with wait/notify).

rounds.name: Design round (LLD, sometimes HLD)
rounds.what: At MTS-2/CS-1 mostly LLD/OOD: class diagrams + partial working code for things like a notification service, in-memory file system, train/movie booking, elevator, chess, autocomplete, config service, rate limiter, garbage collector. Some loops ask schema-first design (DB tables + SQL queries). CS-2 loops add a separate HLD round (file storage, content filter, large-scale services).
rounds.probes: Design patterns by name (strategy, observer, factory, singleton), SOLID, right abstraction (interviewer iterates until satisfied), thread safety, extensibility follow-ups ('add retries', 'change the data type', 'add another channel').

rounds.name: Hiring manager / techno-managerial
rounds.what: Project deep dive (challenges, tradeoffs, your exact role, impact), behavioral (conflict with management, why Adobe, why switch), and almost always 1-2 more coding questions or a small design task — this round is NOT purely behavioral at Adobe.
rounds.probes: Rate-yourself-in-C++/Java and justify it; everything on your resume is fair game; story-framed coding (LRU as a real-world scenario); occasional puzzle.

rounds.name: Director round
rounds.what: Final decision round with a BU director: behavioral (motivation, academics — some directors ask 10th/12th/graduation marks), plus a puzzle (priests & devils, 25 horses, poisoned wine bottles) and/or an open-ended technical task: design/implement a feature of the product (e.g. an Illustrator feature, Acrobat file system), an HLD discussion, or deep infra questions (e.g. RabbitMQ failure handling with repeated 'what if this also fails').
rounds.probes: Senior-engineer judgment: what you look for in a PR or design-doc review; working code is sometimes expected even here (LRU in C++, Dutch national flag in an IDE). Several rejections reported at this stage after 4 positive technical rounds.

process.indiaNotes: Noida is the main hub (Acrobat/Document Cloud and many platform teams), Bengaluru second (Illustrator, Creative Cloud, SDET). India loops are sequential elimination rounds, frequently compressed into one-day drives with results within minutes-hours; US loops are recruiter screen -> tech phone screen -> 4-5 round virtual onsite block with debrief. India rounds leans harder on C++/Java internals, OS/DBMS theory and puzzles than US reports do. Recurring India complaints (2025): interviewer no-shows and multiple reschedules, unresponsive HR after rounds, rejection via feedback that contradicts the candidate's recollection, and offers lost to internal candidates after positive feedback — keep other pipelines warm.
process.timeline: Fast by big-tech standards: 1-3 weeks end-to-end is typical in India (several 2025 offers in 1-2 weeks; single-day drives common); 2 months reported for one 6-round C++ loop. US: 3-6 weeks.
tips: Prepare the C++ pack if the team is C++ (Illustrator/Acrobat/Photoshop): unique_ptr/shared_ptr internals, move semantics, vtable/vptr, singleton (thread-safe + variants), mutex/condition-variable coding, diamond problem, memory leaks — asked in nearly every round.
For every DP problem be ready to code recursive, memoized AND tabulated versions; interviewers explicitly ask for all approaches and for bug-free first-attempt code.

Expect LeetCode-easy/medium difficulty but with variants: interviewers mutate the standard problem (N-ary cousins, negative jumps, k-group with alternating sizes) and expect you to adapt existing code.
Practice story-framed problems: Adobe wraps standard problems (Minimum Height Trees, Top-K Frequent, LRU) in long business narratives — extract the underlying problem fast.
LLD >> HLD for MTS-2/CS-1: drill notification service, file system, booking systems, parking lot, elevator with design patterns named out loud; write runnable class code, not just diagrams.

Prepare the HM/Director rounds like technical rounds: coding and design tasks appear there too, plus puzzles (25 horses, poisoned wine, river crossing) and engineering-judgment questions (what do you check in a PR review).
Know your own project's HLD cold — almost every round opens with it, and one round may be entirely 'draw your project's architecture and defend it'.
State assumptions and clarify output format before coding (one candidate's feedback claimed an unsolved problem over a print-vs-return misunderstanding).
process.notes: OA platform: HackerRank (campus/early-career; occasionally laterals). Live coding: own IDE with screen share, HackerRank CodePair, or shared editor; most interviewers want compiled, tested code. No bar-raiser; no fixed values round — culture fit is assessed in HM/Director rounds. Round content is decided by panels at runtime, so recruiters genuinely can't tell you what's next. Language: C++ teams effectively require C++; Java/backend and frontend (JS/React) loops exist and test those stacks deeply. Role/level can change mid-process (CS-1 -> MTS-2, or a generic 'SDE' posting turning out to be release engineering). Puzzles are a real, recurring component in India manager/director rounds. Lots of 2025 reports of process chaos (reschedules, ghosting, internal-candidate losses) — treat positive feedback as nothing until the offer letter.

dsa.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
dsa.variant: Asked as 'find ALL subarrays whose sum equals K' in a Jul 2026 Noida Computer Scientist screening; interviewer gave no hints.

dsa.title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
dsa.evidence: US tech phone screen 2026-03 (1point3acres); also #8 in Adobe's July-2026 LeetCode tag snapshot

dsa.title: Active users in a sliding time window
dsa.statement: Process a stream of log entries (timestamp, userId, eventType) arriving in increasing time order. At any point, report the number of unique users who generated at least one event in the last 5 minutes relative to the current event's timestamp. Design the data structures so updates and queries stay efficient as old events expire.
dsa.evidence: CS1 ALM-org drive round 1, Nov 2025

dsa.title: Most Stones Removed with Same Row or Column
dsa.variant: Followed by Java concurrency questions (multiple threads modifying a shared list/map) and SQL internals in the same round.
dsa.evidence: CS1 ALM-org drive round 2, Nov 2025

dsa.title: Time Needed to Inform All Employees (+ sequential variant)
dsa.variant: Part 2 variant: messages are passed sequentially to children with +1 time per successive child (CEO at t=0, first child t=1, second t=2 ...) — recompute minimum time.
dsa.evidence: MTS-2 round 1, Nov 2025 — both versions coded

dsa.title: Minimize array sum after K ceil-halving operations
dsa.statement: Given an array of integers, you may perform the following operation K times: remove an element, replace it with ceil(element/2), and put it back. Minimize the final sum of the array. Expected solution: max-heap, always halve the current maximum, O(N log N).
dsa.variant: Variant family of LC 2530 (Maximal Score After Applying K Operations).
dsa.evidence: MTS-2 round 1, Nov 2025; paired with a knapsack-variation DP

dsa.title: K Closest Points to Origin
dsa.variant: Round also covered smart pointers (unique/shared), memory management, constructors/destructors in C++.
dsa.evidence: MTS-2 C++ round 1, Aug 2025

dsa.title: Trapping Rain Water
dsa.variant: Asked as a 'max water trapped' variation (CS1 Aug 2025: brute -> optimal with dry run, then edge-case nitpicking); straight version in MTS-2 Noida Jun 2025 round 1.
dsa.evidence: 2 reports: CS1 round 1 (2025-08), MTS-2 Noida offer round 1 (2025-06); also #2-ranked classic in Adobe's LC tag history

dsa.title: Reverse Words in a String
dsa.variant: With careful multi-space handling, O(n) expected (CS1 2025); also asked for very long strings in an MTS-2 frontend loop (2024); older GfG variant bans loops/length functions.
dsa.evidence: CS1 round 2 (2025-08); MTS-2 frontend round 4 (2024-08); GfG Computer Scientist round 4 (2019)

dsa.title: Find Median from Data Stream
dsa.variant: Two priority queues; pseudo-code accepted; same 70-min round then covered CAP theorem, DB locking, SQL vs NoSQL, normalization, OS locks and an LRU-cache implementation.
dsa.evidence: Release-engineer-track round 1, Jul 2025

dsa.title: LRU Cache
dsa.variant: Recurring in many forms: pseudo-code after median-of-stream (2025-07); in Java with follow-up 'make the eviction algorithm pluggable (LRU/LFU) via strategy pattern' (MTS-2 Noida 2025-06); story-framed real-world scenario in a CS-2 Director round with working C++ code expected (2025-04); LFU-design discussion after a DSA round (CS1 2025); OA design task (CS2 2025-07); thread-safe LRU (SDE2 2023).
dsa.evidence: 6+ reports 2023-2025 across levels and rounds

dsa.title: Friends Of Appropriate Ages
dsa.evidence: Release-engineer-track round 2, Jul 2025; full code + outputs on interviewer's inputs

dsa.title: Jobs on two schedulers + dependency follow-up
dsa.statement: Given an array of job durations and two schedulers that each run one job at a time, compute the minimum time to finish all jobs. Follow-up: jobs now have dependencies — explain how you would schedule them (topological sort) and what happens if the dependency graph has a cycle.

dsa.statement: Given a word set and a list of sentences, two words are interchangeable if they are anagrams. Canonicalize each word (sorted chars) and count group sizes.

dsa.title: Minimize the maximum 'beauty' over K subarray splits
dsa.statement: Split an array into k contiguous non-empty subarrays. A subarray's beauty = (max element) x (length). For a given split, take the maximum beauty across its subarrays; over all possible splits, return the minimum such value. Relative of LC 410 (Split Array Largest Sum) with a max*len cost.
dsa.variant: Candidate explained approach + partial code; interviewer accepted the thought process.
dsa.evidence: CS1 round 1, May 2025 (same round covered vector/list/map internals, vtable, thread-safe singleton, virtual memory, paging)
